topics.getting-started:
graftr — getting started

A Git worktree is a separate checkout of a repository on its own branch.
Graftr prepares its environment and configured hooks; networking and Herdr are optional.
You start your own servers; Graftr does not manage them.

1. Configure a project

   You need Git. The native CLI needs no Bun, Node, Python or external flock.
   Herdr is optional; automatic detection is the default. Standalone setup is synchronous.
   Tailscale is optional: only a configured graftr hook tailscale publisher uses it.
   For workspace integration, run from a Herdr pane in your main repository workspace.

   Add a profile to ~/.config/graftr/projects.json, for example:

   {
      "schemaVersion": 2,
      "herdr": "auto",
     "projects": {
       "my-project": {
         "repo": "/absolute/path/to/repo",
         "worktreeRoot": "/absolute/path/to/worktrees/my-project",
         "localPorts": [3200, 3300],
         "envOverrides": { "PORT": "{{localPort}}" }
       }
     }
   }

   Use your actual absolute paths. PROJECT is the profile name, not a folder path.
   The top-level herdr setting can be omitted (auto), set to off to stay standalone,
   or required to refuse unavailable Herdr. No command flag is normally needed.
   XDG_CONFIG_HOME is honored; a former devtree config is reused until
   graftr migrate --apply renames it. New native worktrees need autoSetup: true to enroll
   automatically; explicit create/setup does not require it.

2. Create your first task

   graftr create my-project fix-login --wait
   graftr list my-project

    TASK is your short task name; by default its branch is task/fix-login and its task ID is
    my-project--fix-login. Later commands also accept the folder name, branch,
    or path; see graftr help targeting. list shows the existing full IDs.
    Project branchName/worktreePath templates can change new branch/folder names,
    not the task ID; see graftr help naming.
   Outside Herdr setup finishes before returning. Inside Herdr use --wait or check status.

3. Start working

   Work in the printed checkout path; optionally use Herdr's shell tabs.
   Install dependencies yourself, or configure an approved installCommand.
   Run your app in a shell on its assigned local port. The profile above
   exports PORT; adapt envOverrides for your app's actual configuration variables.
    This local-only profile needs no Tailscale. Visit your app on localhost.
    For optional publishing commands and a declared URL, see graftr help hooks.

4. Pause or finish

   graftr close my-project--fix-login
   graftr open my-project--fix-login

   close keeps the checkout; open prepares it again at the same path and URL.
   To delete a finished checkout, use remove after saving your work. Its help
   explains the confirmation and deletion safeguards.

More help:
  graftr help create
  graftr help setup
  graftr help remove

Full configuration and machine setup:
  https://github.com/JavanFriedel/graftr/blob/main/README.md
topics.recovery:
graftr — undo and recovery

Diagnose first without changing resources:
  graftr doctor my-project--fix-login
  graftr doctor my-project--fix-login --live
Unknown evidence is not absence; review conditional guidance before recovery.

Unpublish and later restore a task's URL (cleanup hooks, then setup hooks):
  graftr cleanup my-project--fix-login
  graftr open my-project--fix-login

Inspect failed/interrupted cleanup before explicitly retrying cleanup/remove.

Close a workspace, then reopen the same checkout and assigned URL:
  graftr close my-project--fix-login
  graftr open my-project--fix-login

Remove a clean checkout but retain its branch, then resume committed work:
  graftr remove my-project--fix-login
  graftr create my-project fix-login --branch task/fix-login --wait

Use the actual retained branch name from the removal result. This creates a new
checkout and environment; it cannot restore deleted ignored files or guarantee
the same ports. Existing branches must not be checked out or claimed elsewhere.

For deliberate permanent cleanup, nuke removes a clean checkout and its merged
local branch after typed confirmation. There is no automatic undo and no force
override. Use remove if you might want to resume the branch later.

Setup and installation are not general transactions: arbitrary installer side
effects cannot be undone. Existing .env files and shell exports are not rewritten.
If preparation fails, keep the checkout, fix the reported issue, and retry setup.

Read the action's help before running it:
  graftr help cleanup
  graftr help create
  graftr help remove
  graftr help nuke
topics.targeting:
graftr — choosing a worktree

Target-taking commands accept an exact checkout folder name, exact Git branch,
absolute/relative directory path, or existing full PROJECT--TASK identifier:

  graftr open fix-login
  graftr open task/fix-login
  graftr open ../worktrees/fix-login
  graftr open my-project--fix-login
  graftr open fix-login --project my-project

Short names and branches use the current managed project as context. Outside a
known project, a short target must be unique across all managed projects. Use
--project to select a project explicitly. Ambiguous matches are errors; Graftr
never picks the first result or performs fuzzy/prefix matching.

An existing full ID is authoritative. Explicit paths and full IDs can address
another project, unless --project restricts them. Path selection does not rename
or move a checkout, rebind a branch, or enroll an unmanaged worktree.

Without a target, commands use the current managed directory (including nested
directories), then the caller's owned Herdr workspace. @ requests the same behavior.
Native Herdr plugin actions use their selected workspace, not their worker's cwd.
Nuke still requires an explicit target; @ and omitted targets are refused.

Existing ownership, clean-Git and confirmation checks still apply after
selection. A different branch in a recorded checkout must still be reviewed.

Bash command and target completion is installed by normal dotfiles setup.
For custom installations, graftr completion bash prints the same script.
topics.output:
graftr — machine-readable output

Lifecycle and inspection commands accept --json for one versioned result on stdout:
  graftr create my-project fix-login --wait --json
  graftr open fix-login --json
  graftr list my-project --json

The envelope has schemaVersion: 1, command, ok, outcome, data, error, and progress.
This schema version describes CLI output, not persisted task/setup schemas.
Public commands print human-readable summaries by default; use --json for agents
and scripts. Tables adapt to terminal width, moving long columns below each row
or stacking labeled fields without truncating values. Redirected output uses 80
columns unless COLUMNS is set. list --json wraps its inventory in data.
Interactive statuses use green for ready/thawed, yellow for closed/pending,
blue for frozen and red for failures. Set NO_COLOR=1 to disable colors.
Redirected output, TERM=dumb and --json stay plain; status words remain visible.
Update consumers from .worktrees to .data.worktrees (and .project to .data.project).

outcome:
  completed  The requested action finished, including explicitly skipped setup.
  queued     A worker accepted it; use data.logId and graftr status to follow it.
  cancelled  Confirmation was declined; no lifecycle mutation was attempted.
  failed     No tracked lifecycle mutation was attempted, or health checks failed.
  partial    Setup is incomplete/unmanaged, or a mutation was attempted before failure.

Exit 0 and ok: true mean completed, queued, or cancelled. Exit 1 and ok: false
mean failed or partial. Always check outcome; ok alone does not mean ready.
create, setup, and open all fail for incomplete/unmanaged setup, including when
a plain checkout was retained. --no-setup remains an intentional successful skip.

data contains the command result, or null on an exception. Setup results retain
status, step, dependencies, path/workspace, and available timing/log information.
error is null on success; otherwise it has code, message, phase, details, and
recovery guidance. Codes are coarse categories; do not parse message text.

progress lists ordered lifecycle stages attempted by this invocation, each with
action, target, and status (completed or uncertain). Completed means the stage
returned, not that it changed anything or proves the current external state.
Uncertain means it threw: a timed-out request may still have taken effect.
This is not a rollback log; it excludes locks, timing history, and arbitrary
project-script effects. Never automatically undo or retry uncertain steps.

JSON mode does not bypass confirmation, ownership, clean-Git, or merge checks.
Prompts and optional diagnostics remain on stderr; stdout contains only the result.
Help takes precedence and remains text, even with --json. Completion output stays
a shell script; --json is not supported for completion or internal plugin commands.
topics.naming:
graftr — creation paths and branch names

Project profiles can customize new CLI worktrees without changing existing IDs:

  "worktreeRoot": "/absolute/path/to/worktrees",
  "branchName": "feature/{{task}}",
  "worktreePath": "{{project}}/{{branchSlug}}",
  "workspaceLabel": "{{httpsPort}} {{taskName}}"

graftr create my-project fix-login creates branch feature/fix-login at
/absolute/path/to/worktrees/my-project/feature-fix-login. Its ID remains
my-project--fix-login; its workspace label still uses the assigned HTTPS port
and the branch-derived task name with spaces.

Defaults are branchName: task/{{task}} and worktreePath: {{task}}.
Both templates accept {{project}}, {{task}}, and {{repoName}} (main folder name).
worktreePath also accepts {{branch}} (actual full branch, including slashes) and
{{branchSlug}} (flattened ASCII letters/numbers/dots/underscores/hyphens; other runs become
hyphens, repeated hyphens collapse, and edge dots/hyphens are trimmed).
Slug conversion is lossy, not a unique ID: collisions fail, never pick a new suffix.

--branch NAME uses an existing local branch instead of rendering branchName;
worktreePath receives that actual branch. It never fetches or resets the branch.
The configured templates also apply to --no-setup. Missing/unreadable legacy
configuration keeps its existing native fallback; explicit parsed creation settings
must be valid and never silently fall back to Herdr naming.

worktreePath must be a normalized relative path beneath worktreeRoot; subdirectories
are allowed. Absolute paths, traversal, Git metadata, symlinked destinations/parents,
and occupied/claimed/overlapping checkout paths are refused before creation.
Rendered branches must pass Git's exact local branch validation.
Templates are text substitution only: no shell commands, environment lookups, or
expressions. Port/URL/workspace values do not exist at creation time.

Existing managed tasks always reopen at their recorded branch/path. Changing the
templates does not move/rename worktrees, change branches, migrate IDs, or reassign
ports/URLs. Native Herdr worktrees keep their chosen folder and branch. Remove and
create --branch use the current path policy for a fresh checkout; deleted ignored
files are not restored. Removal deletes only the checkout, not empty parent groups.

Full configuration: docs/configuration.md (Creation naming templates).
topics.hooks:
graftr — optional lifecycle hooks and networking

Approved project profiles can declare one hooks object. afterEnvironment runs
before tabs/install; afterDependencies runs before readiness; cleanup runs when
cleaning up, closing or removing the task, including native Herdr post-events.
retire runs only when the task is permanently removed (remove, nuke or native
removal), after its checkout is gone; it is recorded once and kept across
close/reopen, so it suits per-task resources such as databases.

  "hooks": {
    "afterEnvironment": [
      { "name": "report-preparing", "command": ["sh", "-c", "echo preparing"] }
    ],
    "afterDependencies": [
      { "name": "generate", "command": ["pnpm", "run", "generate"], "timeoutMs": 120000 }
    ],
    "cleanup": [
      { "name": "report-closed", "command": ["sh", "-c", "echo \"$GRAFTR_TASK_ID closed\""] }
    ]
  }

Each phase allows up to 16 uniquely named hooks in array order. Names follow the
usual lowercase/hyphen rules. Commands are literal argv arrays, not shell strings
or templates; explicit sh -c allows shell/environment expansion without a helper file.
timeoutMs defaults to 60000 and must be an integer from 100 to 600000.

Omit httpsPorts for local-only tasks. Optional httpsPorts reserves a secondary port;
url declares an HTTP(S) origin template, e.g. http://localhost:{{localPort}}.
Optional "ports": { "api": [3600, 3700] } leases one extra named port per task,
used as {{port.api}} in templates and GRAFTR_PORT_API in hooks.
Declaring a URL publishes nothing; a hook does. Existing tasks keep their recorded
addresses; editing a profile does not reassign ports or URLs.

Private Tailscale URLs use the built-in graftr hook tailscale publisher, which
keeps exact route ownership:

  "url": "https://your-machine.your-tailnet.ts.net:{{httpsPort}}",
  "hooks": {
    "afterDependencies": [{ "name": "publish-tailscale", "command": ["graftr", "hook", "tailscale"] }],
    "cleanup": [{ "name": "cleanup-tailscale", "command": ["graftr", "hook", "tailscale"] }]
  }

It publishes https://HOST:HTTPS_PORT -> 127.0.0.1:LOCAL_PORT, never adopts or
overwrites foreign/changed Serve configuration, and unpublishes only its own route.

Setup hooks run in the verified checkout with inherited environment plus public task
overrides and GRAFTR_PROJECT, GRAFTR_TASK_ID, GRAFTR_WORKTREE_PATH, GRAFTR_BRANCH,
GRAFTR_LOCAL_PORT, GRAFTR_HTTPS_PORT, GRAFTR_PORT_<NAME>, GRAFTR_URL, GRAFTR_HOOK_PHASE, GRAFTR_HOOK_NAME,
GRAFTR_DEPENDENCIES, GRAFTR_SETUP_RUN_ID, GRAFTR_TASK_SLUG (a resource-name-safe
project_folder identifier, also {{taskSlug}}) and, with a retire plan,
GRAFTR_RETIRE_RUN_ID. GRAFTR_* context wins over inherited
or configured assignments; unconfigured optional addresses are omitted, not invented.
Graftr does not source .env into the hook process.
afterEnvironment reports dependencies as pending; it cannot assume an installer
has run. afterDependencies runs even when dependencies are skipped/not configured.

Commands run serially outside the shared registry lock, with stdin closed and
output saved to a private run log (graftr logs). Timeouts terminate only the hook's owned process group. Hooks
must be finite/idempotent: they run again on a new setup/open/retry attempt.
They are trusted code, not a sandbox or an exactly-once transaction. A restarted
interrupted worker can rerun earlier hooks; detached descendants are not contained.

Failure stops later hooks/readiness and retains the checkout/records/leases.
data.hooks and setup receipts show name, phase, observed status, duration and safe
failure reason, never argv/output. A cancelled active hook may finish its own side
effects, but its stale worker cannot run later hooks or publish success.
running is the last observation, not proof a process is still alive.
Review status and fix the issue, then retry setup; arbitrary effects are not undone.

Cleanup commands/public context are recorded before provisioning, and cannot be
retargeted by editing the profile while armed. Cleanup waits for active setup and runs
outside the deleted checkout in private scratch space, under its checkout-operation
lock, never the registry lock. Use PATH/absolute executables and recorded context,
not checkout-relative scripts. GRAFTR_CLEANUP_RUN_ID identifies this provisioning generation
during both setup and cleanup; retries preserve it until cleanup completes.
Successful cleanup commands are skipped until the next setup arms a new generation.
Failed/interrupted cleanup retains ownership/leases; automatic events refuse replay.
Inspect effects before explicitly retrying cleanup/remove. No arbitrary effects are undone.
Status redacts recorded argv/context. Hooks must supply their own external ownership checks.

Configuration, Git branch/ownership, environment, and dependency validity are
rechecked. Hooks cannot silently switch the recorded branch or invalidate managed
assignments/install inputs and still publish ready. No setup hooks run for --no-setup,
unmanaged fallback. Graftr retains the removal handoff/safeguards.
Profiles/records from the retired built-in Tailscale mode must be converted once with
graftr migrate (preview) and graftr migrate --apply; see graftr help migrate.

Full configuration: docs/hooks.md (Unified lifecycle hooks).

adopt.summary: Track an existing worktree without changing its setup
arguments: PATH
Linked Git worktree directory; defaults to the current checkout.
options: Explicitly run the project's dependency installer.
Preview a baseline refresh of an existing private .env; values stay hidden.
Apply the environment preview; back up first and preserve existing differences.
Explicitly replace a differing non-address key; repeat for more keys.
Explicitly run one configured setup hook; repeat to select others.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
adopt.notes:
Default adoption registers the existing path/branch and observes an existing
Herdr attachment and public PORT/BASE_URL from an owner-written root .env when available.
No port allocation, environment writes, installers, hooks, workspace creation or
renaming occurs. Dirty work is allowed and never stashed or committed.
Setup is external, not verified by Graftr. Unknown addresses stay unassigned.
Repeated default adoption is a no-op, including after a failed selected stage.

Stages are independent, synchronous and opt-in on each invocation. Order is environment,
afterEnvironment hooks, installation, then afterDependencies hooks. Hook names alone
are accepted only when unambiguous. No cleanup/retire hooks are armed. Built-in
Tailscale/Postgres publishers require provisioned ownership and cannot be run here;
manual routes/databases are never claimed, changed or deleted by adoption.

--environment without --apply is fully read-only, including the registry. It requires
an existing private untracked .env and an approved separate .env baseline. Preview
first; --apply adds missing non-address keys and only replaces keys explicitly
selected with --take-baseline. Existing public port/URL assignments are protected.
Secret-bearing backups stay outside Git. Existing shell environments are not restarted.
Installers and selected hooks can have arbitrary effects; private logs and stage
results survive failures. Nothing is automatically retried or rolled back.

Adopted worktrees appear in status/list and support logs/doctor. Automatic setup,
open/close/cleanup/removal/freeze operations remain disabled for external setup;
manage the workspace and Git checkout directly. Adoption is tracking, not implicit
conversion to Graftr-provisioned service ownership.

plugin.summary: Install the bundled Graftr Herdr plugin
plugin.notes:
One plugin provides normal worktree actions and worktree.created/opened,
workspace.closed and worktree.removed event hooks. Its startup worker reconciles
owned workspaces and thaws overdue scheduled tasks for that exact Herdr server.
Startup thawing is enabled by default. Set top-level "startupThaw": false in
projects.json to disable only the startup return check, not per-task timers.
There are no plugin targets or install-time behavior flags.
Startup hooks run on future server starts/handoffs, not client attachment or reload.

Writes a private managed manifest under $XDG_DATA_HOME/graftr/plugin (normally
~/.local/share/graftr/plugin), then runs herdr plugin link to enable it for this
user across sessions. Reinstalling refreshes the bundled copy; no source checkout,
network download, sudo, project configuration or running Herdr server is required.
Herdr's CLI must be on PATH. This does not install Graftr or Herdr executables;
Graftr must remain available as graftr on Herdr's PATH.
Does not thaw tasks, create timers, run reconciliation or restart Herdr.
Inspect registrations with herdr plugin list. To unregister without deleting files:
herdr plugin unlink local.graftr.
For editable development links, use herdr plugin link /path/to/plugin instead.
options: Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.

freeze.summary: Reclaim a clean checkout's disk space; retain a frozen recovery record
options: Skip confirmation only; all clean-Git and ownership checks remain.
Opt into a persistent one-off systemd user timer to thaw at this ISO timestamp.
Leave a single-line note for the welcome-back pane (no secrets).
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
examples: graftr freeze fix-login --until 2026-11-06T09:00:00-05:00 --note "Retry after upstream release"
freeze.notes:
Deletes the checkout, including ignored .env, dependencies and caches. Keeps
the observed local branch/commit and a private recovery record, not a backup.
Runs cleanup AND retire hooks; configured task databases may be deleted too.
Save valuable ignored files first. Dirty/untracked work blocks freezing.
Releases ports; thaw regenerates the environment from current configuration.
Use graftr frozen to find stored tasks and graftr thaw TARGET to return.
From inside Herdr, an independent worker finishes after the caller's pane closes;
a freezing response means accepted, not completed. Inspect frozen/status elsewhere.

Scheduling is optional, Linux-only and requires a recorded Herdr attachment plus
a reachable systemd user manager. Dates require an explicit ISO timezone; natural
language dates are not accepted. Persistent per-task unit files survive reboot.
Unavailable Herdr/parent workspaces defer to one-off retries (5 minutes up to 6 hours).
Setup/installer/hook failures require manual review, not automatic replay.
No scheduler is contacted for an unscheduled freeze. See docs/freezing.md.
freeze.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

frozen.summary: List frozen tasks and unfinished freeze/thaw recovery
frozen.notes: Read-only. Frozen records have no port leases and are not expired by prune. Completed thaws leave the frozen listing; status shows their active tasks.
options: Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.

thaw.summary: Recreate a frozen checkout and prepare its environment
options: Thaw manually and synchronously without opening a workspace.
Check overdue scheduled tasks for this exact Herdr server.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
thaw.notes:
Requires an explicit frozen target (full ID, branch, former folder or path).
Keeps the recorded path/branch, allocates new available ports, regenerates .env
and reinstalls dependencies unless installation was explicitly skipped before freeze.
Never resets a missing/moved branch, adopts another checkout or restores ignored files.
Cancels its scheduled timer before setup. Preparation is synchronous; failures keep
the checkout and recovery state for explicit review/retry, not automatic replay.
Attached tasks reopen without stealing focus and receive a welcome-back tab in the
first position, explaining the return date, note and setup result. Existing selection
is preserved. No dev server is started.

--due never returns unscheduled/future tasks or another server's tasks.
The Graftr plugin checks overdue returns at startup by default. Set top-level
"startupThaw": false in projects.json to disable that startup check; an explicit
thaw --due and per-task timers still work. Install with graftr plugin install.
No always-running Graftr daemon or periodic polling. See docs/freezing.md.
thaw.targetNote: TARGET selects a frozen task by former folder, branch, path or full ID. Use graftr frozen to find it.

schedule.summary: Schedule, reschedule or cancel a frozen task's automatic return
options: Future ISO timestamp with timezone; installs a persistent per-task user timer.
Cancel automatic return; leave the task frozen.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
schedule.notes:
Requires a fully frozen task with a recorded Herdr server. Only scheduling
uses systemd; manual freeze/thaw does not require it. Unit files are private and
stored in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user (normally ~/.config/systemd/user).
They invoke this Graftr executable/source entrypoint with explicit config/state paths
and the scheduling shell's PATH, not its secrets or other environment variables.
Reboots preserve the schedule; missed returns run when the user manager starts.
No root service, lingering or waking the computer is enabled. Late is possible.
Cancelling/rescheduling fences stale workers. Inspect graftr frozen for retry/error
state and systemctl --user list-timers for installed timers.
schedule.targetNote: TARGET selects a frozen task by former folder, branch, path or full ID. Use graftr frozen to find it.

create.summary: Create a worktree with its own environment and optional integrations
arguments: PROJECT
A project name from your Graftr configuration.
TASK
A short name using lowercase letters, numbers, and single hyphens.
options: Branch or commit to start from; defaults to the repository's HEAD.
Override configuration and use standalone preparation for this command.
Check out an existing local branch instead of creating the configured branch.
Wait for setup to finish instead of queuing it in Herdr.
Prepare the worktree without installing dependencies.
Create only the checkout (and optional workspace); skip managed setup.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
create.notes:
Works from a plain terminal with Git and a configured project; Herdr is optional.
The top-level herdr setting in projects.json is auto (default), off, or required.
auto checks the contextual connection before mutation; missing/unreachable Herdr
selects standalone preparation. No Herdr executable is needed for that fallback.
off always selects standalone; required refuses missing/unreachable Herdr.
Without attachment (or with --no-herdr), create and setup finish synchronously without
a socket, workspace, tabs, notification, plugin, or background runner. Inside Herdr,
the existing workspace integration and default background setup remain available.
Ownership, permission and invalid-response errors remain errors. There is no fallback
after workspace changes begin, even if the reply is lost; inspect before retrying.
Creates the configured branch (default task/TASK) from committed code,
not uncommitted changes. Project branchName/worktreePath templates customize new
branches and paths beneath worktreeRoot; see graftr help naming.
Project and task names are limited to 48 characters each.
--branch requires an existing, unused local branch. It never fetches, resets,
or force-checks out a branch; choose either --branch or --base, not both.
After remove, use --branch to resume committed work in a fresh checkout.
Deleted ignored files are not restored, and new port assignments may differ.

Herdr-integrated setup runs in the background by default. Check graftr status for completion.
The configured installer may run, but you start your own development servers.
--skip-install persists until you run graftr setup --install.
Repeating create for an existing task reuses its recorded branch, checkout, and
assignments, even after naming templates change. Native Herdr names are retained.

setup.summary: Set up or retry setup in the current linked Git worktree
options: Wait for setup to finish instead of queuing it in Herdr.
Skip dependency installation until --install is requested.
Run the configured installer again and clear the persistent skip.
Prepare the current checkout synchronously without Herdr attachment or calls.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
setup.notes:
Run inside the linked Git worktree you want to prepare; this takes no task ID.
The top-level projects.json herdr mode defaults to auto: use a reachable contextual
Herdr connection, otherwise prepare the canonical checkout synchronously.
off selects standalone; required refuses unavailable Herdr. Plugin actions always
require their selected workspace and never fall back to the worker's directory.
--no-herdr selects the local preparation path without discarding a known attachment.
The checkout must belong to a configured project. Setup prepares the declared
environment, optional Herdr shell tabs, dependencies, and configured hooks, not a server.
Publishing (for example a Tailscale URL) is a configured hook; see graftr help hooks.

Existing environment files and shell exports are not overwritten. If declared
assignments differ, review the worktree's .env before retrying.
Choose either --install or --skip-install, not both.

open.summary: Reopen or prepare an existing managed worktree
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
options: Wait for setup to finish instead of queuing it in Herdr.
Prepare synchronously without opening or contacting a Herdr workspace.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
open.notes:
Preserves the checkout, branch, environment file, and assigned ports/optional URL.
Restores missing shell tabs and reruns provisioning hooks, including any publisher.
Finish outstanding failed/interrupted cleanup before provisioning again.
The top-level projects.json herdr mode defaults to auto; missing/unreachable contextual
Herdr selects synchronous local preparation. off selects standalone, required refuses
unavailable Herdr, and --no-herdr overrides configuration for this invocation.
With Herdr available, an unattached standalone checkout opens/attaches at the
same path with the same ID, environment, receipt and leases; no second checkout.
Fallback never clears a known attachment or retries an uncertain workspace mutation.
Herdr setup runs in the background by default; inspect graftr status for completion.
open.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

list.summary: List a project's worktrees and task IDs
arguments: PROJECT
A project name from your Graftr configuration.
list.notes:
Includes the main checkout, managed tasks, adopted external worktrees, and unmanaged Git worktrees.
Compare setup status with lifecycle state; a folder alone is not proof
that setup finished. Listing never probes servers or removes files.
Invalid record files produce an incomplete report with validated rows and exit 1.
JSON uses outcome partial and data.recordIssues; file contents are never echoed.
When ownership records are invalid, unclaimed checkouts show unknown tracking, not unmanaged.
Preserve damaged records and their leases; listing never repairs or deletes them.
options: Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.

status.summary: Show all managed tasks and their setup results
status.notes:
Shows a readable overview of managed worktrees, setup state and addresses,
plus frozen work, scheduled returns, retries and recovery messages across projects.
Adopted worktrees show adopted/external; no setup success or unknown address is invented.
Project and task names have separate columns; full PROJECT--TASK IDs still work
as command selectors and remain unchanged in JSON output.
Retained logs and backups are reported separately by graftr history.
Use --json for full task records, setup receipts, dependency results, recorded timings
and retained-history details in the versioned result envelope.
Cleanup summaries never include recorded argv or environment context.
Human STATE labels include prepared, closed and resources cleaned;
SETUP completed means the configured setup finished, not that a server is running.
Dependency installation may be explicitly skipped or not configured.
Pending means setup is queued or running. JSON retains the existing status values.
This is recorded state, not a live application health check.
Invalid record files produce an incomplete report with validated rows and exit 1.
JSON uses outcome partial and data.recordIssues; file contents are never echoed.
Preserve damaged records and their leases; status never repairs or deletes them.
options: Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.

history.summary: Summarize retained logs, backups and other historical state
history.notes:
Shows nonempty categories with entry counts, disk sizes and oldest dates.
Reads file metadata only; does not display backup contents, probe services or delete
anything. This is retained storage, not a chronological command audit log.
Counts do not mean every entry is safe to delete; use graftr prune to preview cleanup.
Use --json for category/count/bytes/oldest records under data.retained.
options: Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.

env.summary: Preview or explicitly refresh private development environment values
arguments: refresh
Compare the approved development baseline with this task's existing .env.
TARGET
Managed worktree; omit inside its directory. No Herdr inference.
options: Add missing baseline keys; save a private recovery backup before any change.
Explicitly select an existing differing key to replace; repeat for more keys. Preview-only without --apply.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
env.notes:
Preview is read-only and prints key names/statuses/actions, never values or hashes.
Without historical baseline evidence, different values may be local edits or baseline
changes. Missing keys may also be deliberate omissions: review the preview first.
--apply adds missing keys only; --take-baseline explicitly authorizes selected
replacements. Existing/local-only keys are never removed. Fixed managed port/URL
assignments cannot be selected or changed; profile assignment drift must be reviewed.

Both files must be private owned regular files at canonical non-symlink paths,
at most 4 MiB, with supported unambiguous dotenv syntax. Missing or tracked target
.env files, changed Git ownership and pending setup are refused. Preparing tasks
need an incomplete receipt; apply also refuses an active per-checkout setup lock.
No remote services, project parsers, installers, hooks, health checks or servers run.

Apply saves exact original bytes under the private state directory's env-backups
(outside Git), then rechecks inputs and atomically replaces .env. Selected keys use
the last baseline declaration's raw syntax, replacing the first current occurrence
and removing its duplicates, even when the last value matches. Missing keys are
appended; untouched bytes and unselected duplicates are preserved. Values and shell
references are never expanded or executed. Backup files contain secrets: keep them
private; they survive remove/nuke and follow the history/prune retention policy.
No baseline-provenance/history database or secret hashes are created.

Stop external editors/writers before apply. Graftr locks serialize its own operations,
not arbitrary file writers; there is no atomic transaction across backup and .env.
Interrupted/failed apply may leave only a backup or an already-replaced file; review
progress, the backup and current .env privately rather than automatically retrying.
No automatic rollback or restart: existing shells and applications retain old values.

Exit 0 means preview/apply completed, not that every difference was resolved.
data.reviewRequired identifies differing values deliberately preserved. Errors use
the normal failed/partial JSON envelope; no environment contents are logged.
env.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

doctor.summary: Diagnose a task's recorded resources without changing them
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory, or owned Herdr workspace with --live.
options: Also read workspace inventory from the recorded Herdr server.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
doctor.notes:
Local mode checks checkout/Git registration/branch, ownership records/profile,
and the last setup receipt. It never contacts Herdr, even to select a target:
provide a target or run inside its managed directory.
--live also reads the recorded Herdr server. External effects of hooks, such as a
published Tailscale route, are not verified.
External reads have bounded transport/subprocess timeouts; outages are unknown,
not missing resources. Pending receipts do not prove a worker is still running.

Findings are ok, attention, unknown, or not-checked. Exit 0 means all requested
observations agree; exit 1 means attention or unknown evidence. With --json,
data retains the report on diagnostic failure, outcome is failed (not partial),
error is DOCTOR_ATTENTION or DOCTOR_INCOMPLETE, and progress stays empty.
complete covers requested observations only; local mode leaves live checks unchecked.

No repair, locks/record/lease writes, environment-file reads, project commands,
health checks, application probes, or automatic retry. A ready receipt is historical
evidence, not current environment/dependency/application verification. Reports are
point-in-time observations, not atomic snapshots. Review conditional next steps
before deliberately using setup/open/cleanup; preserve uncertain effects.
doctor.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

health.summary: Run a task's explicitly configured application checks
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
health.notes:
Runs only the project's approved healthChecks and prints a readable report.
Use --json for the full structured result.
HTTP/TCP checks use the assigned local port, not a published URL.
With a directory or explicit target, a live Herdr connection is not required.

No configured checks reports not-configured, not unhealthy. Exit status is
nonzero for unhealthy results or invalid requests. This never starts servers,
changes lifecycle records, or schedules recurring checks.
options: Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
health.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

close.summary: Clean up configured resources and close the optional workspace; keep files
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
close.notes:
Runs recorded cleanup hooks (for example unpublishing a URL) and closes
any attached Herdr workspace/panes. Cleanup waits for active setup outside the registry lock.
Keeps files, the branch, and port assignments so graftr open can restore it.
Unattached tasks need no Herdr connection. Detached or external servers are not stopped.

Closing from inside an attached workspace hands off to Herdr's independent worker. A closing receipt
means accepted, not completed; inspect graftr status from another workspace.
Herdr's own native close is separate: its post-event hook records closure before
auxiliary cleanup. A cleanup failure retains ownership and is reported in the plugin
log without changing the already-completed native operation.
options: Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
close.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

cleanup.summary: Run recorded cleanup; keep the workspace and files
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
cleanup.notes:
Cancels/fences setup, waits for active setup, and runs recorded cleanup hooks
outside the checkout and registry lock, such as a configured publisher's cleanup.
Keeps the Herdr workspace, checkout, branch, port assignments, and servers.
Use open/setup to reprovision.
Successful cleanup commands are skipped on retry. After failed/interrupted cleanup,
inspect effects before explicitly retrying; automatic events never blindly replay it.
Failures retain ownership/leases.
options: Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
cleanup.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

label.summary: Refresh the owned workspace label from its current Git branch
arguments: TARGET
Managed checkout; omit inside its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
label.notes:
Updates only the live owned Herdr workspace's display label using its current
attached branch and the project's workspaceLabel template. Defaults use the secondary
port prefix when assigned, otherwise the local port. Dirty work is allowed; detached/unregistered/foreign checkouts and
ambiguous workspace ownership are refused. It requires a Herdr attachment and will
not open a closed workspace.

No setup, environment reads/writes, install, hooks, Git rename/move, aliases,
or ownership-record changes. Active/pending setup is refused. Other commands retain
their recorded-branch checks; refreshing the label does not rebind the task.
Target with the folder/path/full ID or recorded branch, not the new display name.
The explicit Herdr action uses its selected workspace, never another client's focus.

This is one-shot, not a background branch watcher. A branch/ownership change or
failed request can leave an already-updated label; inspect Herdr and refresh again.
JSON progress records refresh-label, including uncertain requests. No automatic
rollback or retry. Unchanged labels return without a rename request.
options: Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
label.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

remove.summary: Delete a clean worktree folder; keep its Git branch
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
options: Skip confirmation only; all ownership and clean-Git checks remain.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
remove.notes:
Asks for confirmation, runs recorded cleanup, closes the workspace, deletes the
checkout, and releases its ports. The Git branch is retained.
Uses the current verified attached branch, even after switching away from the
original recorded branch. Confirmation shows both names and the current commit;
switching branches or changing that commit after confirmation requires reconfirmation.
All existing branches are retained. Detached checkouts still require manual review.
Results name the observed branch and include recordedBranch when different. When
both checkout and registration are already absent, branch is null: the last branch
cannot be inferred. Historical ownership records are not rewritten to adopt a branch.
Nuke remains strict about the recorded branch and merge checks.

Resume observed commits with create PROJECT TASK --branch BRANCH. This creates a new
environment and lease; it cannot recover deleted ignored files.

WARNING: Ignored files, including .env, node_modules, and caches, are deleted.
Save anything you need first. Tracked changes and untracked files block removal;
--yes never bypasses those checks, and there is no --force option.
Noninteractive removal requires --yes unless invoked by an explicit Herdr action.

Removal from inside an attached task hands off to Herdr's independent worker; a
removing receipt means accepted, not completed. Unattached tasks remove directly,
even from inside; your shell may remain in the deleted directory, so cd elsewhere.
A known attachment still requires server/ownership checks; --no-herdr is not a
deletion bypass. Detached/external servers remain your responsibility.

Herdr's native force removal remains Herdr's decision, not this command's policy.
Its post-event cleanup fences setup and waits for the setup lock before releasing
leases, then rechecks checkout/Git disappearance. It does not kill installers or
replay deletion. Failed cleanup or late writes retain ownership for review.
remove.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

nuke.summary: Delete a clean worktree and its fully merged local branch
arguments: TARGET
An explicit managed worktree; omission and @ are refused.
nuke.notes:
Run from a terminal outside the target folder and Herdr workspace.
Requires typing the exact branch name and answering a final confirmation.
There is no --yes or --force bypass, and plugin actions cannot skip confirmation.

The branch must be merged into the main checkout's current branch, named in
the confirmation: either its commits are in that history, or (after a squash
merge) merging it would change no files. Git's upstream merge check is also
honored. Protected
main/default branches and branches used by another worktree/task are refused.
Dirty, locked, detached, or ownership-conflicted worktrees are also refused.

WARNING: Deletes the local branch and the entire checkout, including ignored
.env, node_modules, and caches. Remote branches are untouched. There is no
automatic undo; prefer remove when you want to keep the branch.

This is not atomic across Git, Herdr, and disk. If a later step fails, records
and leases remain for review and retry. After fixing the reported issue, run
nuke again and reconfirm; it can finish cleanup after a partial deletion.
options: Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
nuke.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

reconcile.summary: Clean up resources for managed workspaces that are no longer open
reconcile.notes:
Checks recorded tasks against their Herdr workspaces and runs queued cleanup
hooks. Failed/interrupted hooks need an inspected explicit retry.
Does not delete checkouts, release retained port leases, or stop servers.
Standalone tasks are skipped; not having a workspace is normal for them.
An unreachable Herdr connection is not treated as a closed workspace.
options: Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.

migrate.summary: Convert retired built-in Tailscale profiles and records to hooks
options: Back up privately, then convert. Without it, only preview.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
migrate.notes:
Profiles with httpsPorts but no url/hooks gain the tailnet url and the
publish-tailscale/cleanup-tailscale hooks (graftr hook tailscale). originsKey and the
retired default assignments become explicit envOverrides; setupHooks becomes hooks.
Records move to task schema 4. Tasks owning a route hand it to an armed cleanup plan
with an exact route receipt, so the next cleanup/close/remove unpublishes it.

Tailscale Serve, .env files, ports, URLs, workspaces and checkouts are not changed.
Recorded hosts stay authoritative; a project without records asks Tailscale for this
machine's name. Unfinished legacy cleanup or ambiguous hosts block the whole apply.
Backups of projects.json and each converted record go to the private state
directory's migration-backups. Rerunning finishes an interrupted apply.
Upgrade every graftr executable sharing this state first: older builds refuse
schema 4 records. Config/state directories still named devtree are renamed to
graftr last, leaving a devtree symlink for processes that already resolved them.

logs.summary: List a task's private installer and hook output logs
arguments: TARGET
Managed worktree; omit in its directory or owned Herdr workspace.
options: Print the newest log's contents instead of the list.
Limit the target to this configured project.
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
logs.notes:
Each installer and setup/cleanup/retire hook run writes its stdout and stderr to
a private log (0600) under the state directory's logs/<task-id>/. Output is never
copied into CLI results, JSON, status or Herdr notifications; failure messages name
the log's path instead. Logs may contain whatever those commands print, including
secrets, so --latest prints only when you ask, and never with --json.
Each log is cut at 4 MiB and each task keeps its 50 newest.
logs.targetNote: TARGET accepts a checkout name, branch, path, or full ID. See 'graftr help targeting'.

prune.summary: Preview or delete old history, backups and logs from private state
options: Only entries untouched for longer than this (default 30).
Print a versioned result envelope; see graftr help output.
prune.notes:
Graftr already expires this history by itself: once a day, the first lifecycle
command deletes entries older than 30 days. prune clears things sooner or with a
different cutoff, and previews by default. Covers env refresh backups (which hold
secrets), migration backups, run logs, stale creation intents, cleanup scratch
directories, and records of removed tasks and timing samples left by earlier versions. Tailscale and Postgres hook receipts are
deleted only when no current task uses them and every route or database they record
is gone; otherwise they are listed as kept. Task records, setup receipts and lock
files are never pruned, and unrecognized entries are listed and left alone.
graftr status reports each category's count, size and oldest entry.

hook.summary: Run a built-in hook command from a project profile
arguments: tailscale
Publish (afterDependencies) or unpublish (cleanup) the task's private HTTPS URL.
postgres
Copy the dev database into the task's own (afterEnvironment) or drop it (retire).
hook.notes:
Intended for profile hooks, not interactive use: it reads the GRAFTR_* context
that setup/cleanup provide and refuses a stale or foreign generation.
The task needs a secondary httpsPorts lease and a url of https://HOST:{{httpsPort}}
matching this machine's Tailscale name. Requires Tailscale Serve operator access.
Route receipts live in the private state directory's tailscale-hooks and remain
ownership evidence; do not delete them to force adoption.

postgres reads DATABASE_URL from the profile's envSource baseline, creates
<db>_<taskSlug>, copies the dev database into it with pg_dump, and writes one
DATABASE_URL/POSTGRES_DB assignment each in the worktree's private .env, replacing
old declarations and removing their duplicates without expanding unrelated values.
Add it to both hooks.afterEnvironment and hooks.retire; retire drops only a database
it created and never one still in use. Close and cleanup keep the database. Raise
its timeoutMs for large databases. See graftr help hooks.

completion.summary: Print a shell completion script for custom installations
arguments: bash
Generate completion for Bash; other shells are not yet supported.
completion.notes:
Prints a Bash completion script; it never edits your shell configuration.
Install it explicitly for your user, for example:
  mkdir -p ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions
  graftr completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/graftr

Completion reads managed worktree metadata and, for creation options, local Git
refs. It never connects to Herdr or runs setup, project scripts, hooks, or servers.
Missing or invalid state produces no dynamic suggestions or diagnostic noise.
